raw_answer_text:
A1: A "Unicast RIB" (unicast routing table) lookup is performed.
A2: NOT STATED explicitly, but the check is built around the packet's source address — the lookup is for "the route back to the source," implying the source address is the key.
A3: NOT STATED.
A4: It compares that route's interface against the interface on which the packet actually arrived (the ingress interface, e.g., "Ingress ge-0/0/1").
A5: The lookup happens first, then the comparison (the verdict/decision) follows it.
A6: The packet passes when it "Arrived on the 'upstream' interface" — the router then accepts and forwards it.
A7: The packet fails when it arrived on an interface that is not the route back to the source — the router then drops it ("Drop (RPF fail)").
A8: Because the check walks backwards along the path the packet arrived on, using the route toward the source rather than the route toward the destination — that backward orientation is what makes it "reverse."
